utterances.text: So in spite of that heavy burden that had been placed upon you by none other than the president and the supreme commander, as you sit here today you're stating that even had you known that a meeting was taking place five steps away from your office, you would not have attended. That is your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could fast forward a little bit, but you may --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait, wait. I am expecting you to continue so that we can clarify that. In a conversation with Karadzic on the 11th in the evening, I suggested to the president to convey to Mr. Mladic that he should get in touch with me because it seemed really impolite to me, and I was not in a position to find him or to get in touch with him or to oblige him for any kind of meeting, which Karadzic to a certain degree accepted and said, very well, we'll see about that. I did not return to the office to waste my time there for no reason, but we were trying to have a meeting at the office with the people who happened to be there. I already said that I was trying to get in touch with Mladic. At that point in time, it was difficult to find where he is and to get in touch with him. So I concluded that he would -- in any case, he would call me, that he would get in touch with me regarding the orders that I had from Karadzic, and this happened on the 12th, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just expanded on this because you are simplifying this, just so that you would have a more complete picture about it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going step by step, Mr. Deronjic. We're going to get to that. But I just want to fast forward to another statement regarding the same issue here. And this is your statement that was given to you on 21 October 1999, which I believe is marked for identification purposes as 692. Now, before I make reference to the particular section, let us remind ourselves that in between the interview that you had with Mr. Ruez on February 4, 1998, and this interview on October 21, 1999, there was an attempt by Mr. Ruez to have another statement from you back on July 1, 1998. And that -- I'm referring to what has been marked for identification purposes as D94/1. Do you remember that encounter? That was the one time you were informed that you were a suspect. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember most of those meetings, more or less, but I cannot say that I remember the contents without the transcript. I didn't really study them at any point, so if you can provide me with a statement, yes, I can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yesterday we did establish that when you met Mr. Ruez for the second time and you learned that you were a suspect, you made particular inquiries as to what specific portions of your previous statement, what elements of that previous statement, were responsible for the changing of your status. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was naive of me to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It couldn't hurt, right? Who knows, maybe another investigator might have been willing. But as a good investigator, he did not. And you, wanting to protect your own rights, not knowing what might be lurking out there, what dangers you might be placing yourself into, decided not to give a statement, as was your right. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is correct. I should perhaps like to refresh my memory with respect to that, but in principle I agree with what you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the next encounter after July 1st, 1998, is October 21, 1999. And I take it during that period of time, knowing now that your status had changed from witness to suspect, surely you must have taken some steps to learn as much information as you could so that in the next encounter, might there be one, you would be able to provide explanations that would somehow lift this burden from you, that is the status of suspect. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right - and you've just reminded me of me that - I undertook a number of steps. One of them being cancelling the power of attorney of my lawyers. I informed Mr. Ruez of this formal cancellation, and I told him that I would give the next statement alone, on my own. I'm not going to give you the reasons. I assume there is information circulating around to that effect, but that's not important. Second, I decided not to give any interviews in any official offices, official premises, which I suspected of being taped, and I suggested that the next interview be held in Bratunac, which Mr. Ruez accepted. I wanted to be sure that the meeting would not be taped and that information would not leak from that meeting. So this is the next step that I took, if we are talking about the same meeting, and I think we are. And Mr. Ruez agreed with me because I had drawn his attention to the issue of security during the breaks and to the information, which in my opinion had to remain protected. So I did whatever I could in order to learn as much as possible regarding those events, but I have to say that this was not easy. It's not even easy today, let alone at that time. But mainly, for reasons of security, I made an effort to learn as much as possible. To what extent I was successful, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact when Mr. Ruez begins the interview, after the initial formalities - and I'm quoting from page 2, lines 6 to 7 in the Srpski version; lines I believe it's 9 to 11 in the English version - Mr. Ruez begins by asking you or by stating: "I assume you studied it." Okay. Let me wait. And in fact, I'm going to go back up a couple of lines. Page 2, if you could -- I'm going to start with line 2 to 3. And in the English version it would be line 6, page 2 -- line 5. Mr. Ruez says: "Perfect. So it's now 1.26 hours and we are going to start our interview. I don't intend ask you at this point questions. I provided you last time the transcript -- the draft transcript of the first interview that we had together." And then he goes on to state -- apparently he's shown you or you've shown him the transcript. "Yes, this one. I assume you've studied it attentively and maybe now you want to make some comments on what you said at that time. Feel free to discuss whatever you want about the content what you have already said to me." Do you recall Mr. Ruez making that comment to you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it at that point in time when you were having this interview you had indeed studied attentively your previous statement in order -- in preparation for this particular interview. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How it worked in practice was that he was supposed to bring this with him. I don't know exactly when it was I received the transcript, but yes, I agree with your statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to make sure that Mr. Ruez was fair with you. And it would appear to me from reading this that he was indeed very fair. Because in advance he gave you, as he had promised from before, a full translated transcript of your interview so you could look at it, study it, maybe even conduct some investigation, so on the next encounter you could be as precise and as truthful as honest and as complete as you could be. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course you knew now even more importantly than before, since now you were a suspect, that everything that you said might be used at The Hague at some later point, if not against you, perhaps against somebody else. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we are to go on into page 3 of your statement, you indicate - and I'm referring to a portion, it's around line 21 to 26. In the English version it's around 21. I'm not going to quote it completely, but if you look at it it states that you began to formulate a chronology of the events. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 3?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3. I believe it should be on line 21 to 26. You state, and I'll read the English version. "Actually, what I warned you last time, expressed you last time we have a meeting, that I was unprepared for that meeting in the sense of dates and chronology of the events, because I never dealt with any kind of writing of the chronology during the time in question, but after, following our talks, I took it more seriously and more seriously I checked certain dates, but I have to say people are very much unwilling to talk about this. It is very hard to check such things in the archives of the police or the army. So I mainly used some friendly connections, and based on the recollections of those people, we made a chronology, a certain chronology, of the events." Do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you kindly read on, please. If anything is not 100 per cent sure, I should like this to be admitted as well. But I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot find the portion that the witness is reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, I will get to that. I'm just trying to lock you into your position step by step, korak po korak, to use your language. Step by step we're going to get there --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But please --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, did you make that statement that you and your friends made a chronology, yes or no? That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot take a sentence out of the context of the entire passage and have it have the same meaning. I hope that this chronology would be clear one day and that we would have an opportunity to issue -- to state our position with respect of that. So I think that I was in a position to state the chronology of the events at the time. But you must admit, it was difficult for me because I had relied upon the contacts with some friends who were willing to provide me with assistance of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I may add one more point, the following sentence also. What would be absolutely right are the allegations concerning segments of the events. I think that this is more important now than the precise chronology itself, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Deronjic, I would grant you the right to be off on some dates. You can have that, but that wasn't the purpose of my question. Okay? Whether the allegations are more important than the chronology, that's for others to decide. But for right now I just want a clear answer. Did you and other people, your friends, your friendly connections, get together in order to make a chronology for this momentous occasion, that is the giving of a formal statement as a suspect to Mr. Ruez, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to some people. So in regard to that, the answer is affirmative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, may I ask, because I don't think it was asked by

utterances.speaker: MR. RUEZ
utterances.text: Who are these friendly connections? Who are these individuals, and what, in fact, were they able to provide you, either in documents or through their memories?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to my close associates and ordinary people who were able to help me at the time. First of all, Mr. Simic, Davidovic, Vasic, whom I asked at one point about the chronology of these events. I did not recall other people whom I asked for this assistance at the time. But those were the individuals I had in mind, plus Josipovic, for instance, and a number of other people from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the names you just provided us, those are your close and personal associates, all members of and participants in SDS politics at that period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to clarify which period the interview or the 1995. I think I know what you mean, but the record doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were your close assistants during the period of Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, they're probably -- if I'm not wrong, they're probably your boyhood friends, you grew up together?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were they still involved in SDS politics during that period of time when you gave this interview?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated names of a number of people. I don't know who you have in mind. President Simic, I don't know -- I don't think he was president of the municipality any longer, nor was Mr. Davidovic. Vasic, I think, was still the chief of the centre, but Kopalovic [phoen] from Srebrenica, for instance, I think was no longer holder of the same office as during the war. I don't know. Ask me the precise -- the specific question, and I will try to respond as best as I can, if this is important at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Nonetheless, these people whose names you mention, and they crop up during the interviews, were prominent - and I underscore the word "prominent" - members of the SDS party during the events surrounding Srebrenica, the fall of Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not correct nor were they all members of the SDS. To what extent they are prominent, I don't know; some are and some are not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they members of the War Presidency at any point?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, I've given the names of a number of people; some were not, and some were members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of those people members of the Crisis Staff? See, I adjusted my question.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Bratunac, in 1992? In 1992, the only member of the Crisis Staff from the people you've mentioned was Mr. Simic. The others whom I mentioned were not members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your meetings with the Prosecution, the Office of the Prosecution, is it not correct that on occasion with respect to events or chronology, you would ask the investigator to check with those people with respect to dates, because they might be able to be more helpful. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to vagueness at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's been a lot of people mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: People mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- I object. The gentleman can, can -- understood the question. I'm surprised and shocked that the Prosecutor would want to withhold the truth in this case. I am shocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you have to allow the Prosecutor to finish his objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the witness, Your Honour, says that -- which ones, I would then go ahead and give him the specific information. The Prosecutor, had he read these documents, would know that this gentleman on occasion says, Go check with Mr. Davidovic, go check with Mr. Simic. These are the people that he's mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let Mr. McCloskey finish his objection first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karnavas is correct in that, as I recall, Mr. Deronjic did during his many, many interviews sometimes refer investigators back to speaking to specific individuals. There was a number of those individuals. He has recently listed off a whole number of individuals, and a question that is that vague without giving some -- reining in the names or at least with the groupings is too vague for the answer to make any sense and it's an unfair question to be able to ask the witness. If he can make it more specific, I agree with Mr. Karnavas, Mr. Deronjic did say these things. If he can make it more specific to the names, I have no objection. But the question as it is framed is really impossible to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not a fact, Mr. Deronjic, that on several occasions during many of your meetings with the Prosecution you have referred to some of these friendly connections, the ones that you talked about, you referred the Prosecution to your friendly connections to double check the chronology of the events?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I talked about it a number of times. I don't know exactly when. I don't know exactly with respect to whom, but I did state names of individuals likely who were able to provide that kind of information. I cannot tell you exactly when, at what time, and which specific individuals. I would have to be reminded of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But assuming, as you state here, that you met with these friendly connections and based on your collective recollections, we, being all of you, made a chronology, a certain chronology, of events, would it not stand to reason that part of the purpose for you referring the Office of the Prosecution to these friendly connections would be so that they would vouch for your chronology or your participation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I refer the Prosecutor to those individuals if they wanted to learn more and in more detail with respect to the things which I could not remember or was not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at some point in time, as I understand it from reading from your testimony, documents were destroyed relating to certain events. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I once stated that I don't remember exactly when, that is that portion of that documentation that had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you have also indicated that you had learned from Mr. Momir Nikolic that he, on his own initiative, had destroyed documents as well. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the documents that were destroyed that were in the possession of the civilian authorities, would it not be fair to characterise them as members of this group of friendly connections, not all but some?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, some of the members that you had consulted, your friendly connections. Okay. Are they also not the same -- some of the same individuals that were involved in intentionally destroying documents so they would never fall into the hands of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let me explain. In the SDS in late 1995, changes took place. I resigned to the position of the SDS president. A new leadership was elected. At the time, recommendation from higher levels was received to the effect that the documentation should be destroyed. And then from Sarajevo Vidomir Banduka was the president of the SDS. I don't know if he was the one who destroyed the documentation, but I had managed to find it. It is here. This is the complete documentation, so it has not been destroyed. For the military -- the municipal part, I don't know. I don't know because the people I enumerated, such as Mr. Davidovic, were not there at the municipality, nor did they have any function within the military at the time. So I don't know. And I don't know what the situation was with the military, except for what Mr. Nikolic told me. But this can all be checked. Who were the people who held positions within the SDS at the time this recommendation or order came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's move on to your -- to the next segment of your statement. And again, we're going over the same material. You state on page 4, line 8 to 13, this is in the Srpski version. And it's page 4, line -- it starts with line 8. It states -- you begin by saying: "In that sense I want to begin by the contact I had with Karadzic. Physical contact that began after the fall of Srebrenica. Actually, the moment that I have heard about my being appointed for the civil commissioner through the radio -- on the radio. So I went -- following that, I went to the headquarters of the local brigade to get in telephone contact with Mr. Karadzic." Now, further down you state on line 20 to 22 in your version, page 4. And it starts with line 21 in the English version. "I asked him to send me in written form, and then he agreed on my urgent, you know, trip to Pale, that very day. So in the night between the 11th and 12th, I was on Pale -- in Pale. I met with President Karadzic in the Presidency palace." Now, do you see that in the Srpski version?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it would seem to me that now that you've had an opportunity to meet with your friendly connections and to come up with a chronology - an opportunity that had not presented itself the first time you met with the Office of the Prosecution - now the chronology is that in fact on the night between 11th and 12th, based on your urgent requests wanting to know exactly what your role and function was, you went to Pale and you met with President Karadzic. That's what you told Mr. Ruez back then. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct that I stated that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it before stating that, you had time to reflect to make sure that at least with this particular aspect you were going to be as complete as you could be. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the trip between Bratunac and Pale is I think around 140 kilometres, give or take a kilometre or a bump here and there. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those days it would have been a -- I don't want to say a lengthy journey but a significant journey. It's not like going to Potocari which is only 5 kilometres away, you would actually have to be in the car for a couple of hours. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course during that period of time, given your status, and now with your special status, I would suspect - and correct me if I'm wrong - that you had a driver to take you there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the 11th, and we have already established that this is not the correct date. When I went to see Karadzic, which was on the 14th, a piece of information I was able to establish later on, I had a driver, an escort. And I believe I've already provided a detailed description of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a driver available to you on July 11th, 1995, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had my local driver who drove me, but it wasn't an official driver or anything. I just asked him to be available for me over those few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we were to go on to the next page, it says that -- I'm reading here now from page 5. And in your version it would be lines 5 to 10, which apparently correspond with the English version. I'm going to read the English version as it's stated here. There might be an omission, and so please bear with me. I will insert it. "In our assessments, the president and myself, we relied on the good will of the army and police, you know, to carry out the task." I'm told in the Srpski version it also includes: "Of course we did not have instruments for ordering relationships." Is that in your version?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Of course we didn't have any instruments for any kind of order issuing relationship," this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's not in the transcript. Thank you. Now we have an official translation. And then you go on to say: "I had no authorisation to order anything to them. You can clearly see from the paragraph 5 because his decision are actually obliged to be carried out just by civilian authorities and that they were obliged to follow my decision, to act according to my decisions." Do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I know it states that here, but I'm asking you whether you recall making that statement.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you made that statement, was that a honest statement, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer to the question correct or not correct. What does it mean "honest"? It was an incorrect statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise, Mr. Deronjic. I'm trying to move it along so I can get you off the stand in five days, but go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To finish in five days? Look, we are constantly discussing the 11th. I am trying, and I hope you understand that, but it seems to me like you are repeating your mistake. I am saying that that is not the correct date when I went to Pale. Since you are asking me, I will now --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic. I'm sorry. I don't mean to cut you off. We're not discussing whether now you think you didn't go on the 11th or not. I'm talking about this particular statement that you made. Okay? We've already heard your explanation. In your statement here you state: "In our assessment, the president and myself, we relied on the good will of the army and the police, you know, to carry out our tasks." And then you say because you did not have any instruments to order these relationships. Was that a correct statement, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context that this was happening on the 11th in Pale that we were personally talking about, that is an incorrect statement. President Karadzic and I spoke on the telephone on the 11th in the evening and discussed these things over the telephone. So it means that I am not questioning the contents of what I said, but it is incorrect that I discussed that directly with him at Pale on the 11th. A part of these discussions were also conducted on the 14th when I was in Pale about the duties regarding Srebrenica, about how I should proceed, carry out my duties, things relating to UNPROFOR, the means that they had at their disposal, the evacuation of UNPROFOR, the workers of UNPROFOR, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, you've told us all of that. That's not in dispute. But here you're stating that you and the president, the commander and chief of the military, and also the president for the civilian -- the entire country, right, relied on the good will. In other words, he was not in a position, neither he nor you, to order the military, to order the army or the police, but it was basically you had to supplicate to them, beg them to cooperate. Is that what you're trying to suggest to Mr. Ruez that was happening at that period of time? Is that your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that the president had to beg them because he wasn't even able to do that. He wasn't out on the ground and didn't have the opportunity to get in touch with them. I am saying again I was not in a position to issue orders; this is clear to the president. Also that I did not have the instruments nor the order-issuing relationship neither did anyone authorise me to issue orders to the military. This is what I'm talking about. And when we're talking about my function, we are aware, both the president and myself, that I do not have an order-issuing function to the military and the police, but it is implied, it is understood, that they would listen to the constructive proposals that I would put forth in particular because they came from the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, let's get one thing straight, the police fall under the civilian side, do they not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In all states, that they belong to the appropriate ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On paragraph 5 it says here: "Decisions by the civilian commissioner shall be binding for all civilian authority organs." And that would include, would it not, the police, that you had the power to order the police, including the special police. Does it not -- is it not implied in this particular decision, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you say that you didn't -- you were not in a position to order the military, and I believe you are quite correct, at least if we are to look at this that there's nothing in here that gives you, grants you, that right. Paragraph 5, I'm referring again to exhibit P687. This is the decision of your appointment as civilian commissioner. I grant you that. On the other hand, if we go back to paragraph 4, it is clear that you have an overriding obligation, responsibility, and the authority from the president for the well being of everyone. And that's not in dispute, is it, Mr. Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I did not have that decision in front of me when the president and I were talking or the next day, so I don't know what it states. That is why I asked the president to send it to me in writing. And as for whether the president can order me to order the police, that would mean the violation of the regulations and the constitution of Republika Srpska, especially the police, in particular the special police which had had its own command structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we won't get into the legalities of that right now, but let me fast forward a few days past this period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since you are changing the subject, can we have our break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's a quite inopportune time, Your Honour. But nonetheless if it's time for the break, it's time from the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, before we left off before the break, we were talking about your powers, in particular to order be it the police or the military. And I believe that we established that you did have, in fact, the power to order civilian organs, not necessarily the military organ. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. I will give you another example, it relates to the police --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the answer is you cannot, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't want examples, Your Honour. If his answer is that he had no authority to order the civilian authorities, the police being one of them, I accept that answer. There's no need for examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe that example is related to what Mr. Deronjic is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The example refers to this assertion whether I had the authority or not to command the police. I will give one example which shows clearly what my powers were and in which way I was contacting the police. From the transcript of my interview, my last interview to the Prosecution, I am talking about the conversation between myself and Karadzic after the Fontana meeting on the 12th of July. So after this meeting was finished, I went to my office and I called President Karadzic in order to inform him about the Fontana meeting and I also told him about my intentions, what I wanted to do once it was possible for me and my associates to enter Srebrenica, expecting the civilian transports to finish on that or the next day. I gave my statement about that to the Prosecution. So I am telling him of my intentions. Amongst other things, I told him about my intention to form a police cell, which would urgently enter Srebrenica, and then later this unit, this small unit, which I wished to form, would be expanded and then would link up to the Interior Ministry. These plans of mine that the president approved, he, President Karadzic, issues an order to the Minister of Internal Affairs, Tomislav, I can't remember his last name right now. He issued an order to Mr. Vasic to get in touch with me and to act in accordance with his order. So he was giving the authority to the chief of the Zvornik security centre, Mr. Vasic, who at the time was in Bratunac, to get in touch with me. And of course there is also a document which testifies to this fact, and that is a report by Mr. Vasic which I also had the opportunity to see recently from the Prosecution where he informs about receiving the order and acting in accordance with the order and getting in touch with the civilian commissioner with the intention of forming a police unit which would enter Srebrenica. This shows without doubt in which way I could issue orders to the police. So I would contact the president, President Karadzic. President Karadzic, if he agreed with my suggestion would issue an order to the minister, to the minister to the security services' centre, to chief and then the chief would contact me. So what Mr. Karnavas is trying to suggest, that I could issue direct orders to the police, then why would I go this other way? I could simply say, Mr. Vasic, I am ordering you to come to my office and that we could form a police unit. So it's obvious in this example how de facto and de jure also, this institution functioned which was established for the first time in our area, the function of the civilian commissioner. And that is how I acted and I also think that I acted in accordance with the law as well as with my de facto authorities and powers. I think this is a very obvious example and this is why I insisted on telling you about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll stick with that for a second. Earlier you had indicated that when you learned that there were separations going on at Potocari, you asked Vasic to contact Mladic because you were too busy or unwilling to go into Potocari and find Mladic. And you asked Vasic to tell Mladic that this should stop. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how is it that you asked Vasic on that occasion and you did not pick up the phone to call Karadzic, with whom you had a very, very close relationship with and with whom you could visit even unannounced. Why didn't you call him then and say, Mr. President, contact Mladic and tell him to stop. Why did you go through Vasic on that occasion, where killings are going on?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that you are trying to be very suggestive. First, if -- I'm not saying that this is a minor thing, but for any intention of mine I had to pick up the phone and call the president, I would not put the phone down ever. These were some things that were resolved as we went along. I suggest to Vasic; I did not order anything to him. And he listens to me. How could I tell President Karadzic from my office quite openly, you know, Mr. Karadzic your, or our army in Srebrenica and in Potocari is violating the conventions relating to the conduct of war and so on. Do you think that this is possible? Of course it can be done that way as well, but I prefer not do it that way. I think there's no need for me to tell you what my reasons are. I think it is absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to mention, I did not have sufficient information in order to be able to say, Yes, it is true that they are violating customs or war. But it is true that I did say, Could you ask Mladic to stop. And later he informed me that he did convey that to Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, since you were so insistent on giving us an example about de facto and de jure, might I put an example to you and perhaps you might be able to assist us. We're not going to go into the greatest of detail at this point, but I would like to refer to you of the evening of the 13th. And we're going to discuss that in the greatest of detail, but just as a way of example. You have testified on previous occasions, and there are some conflicting views, but you have testified nonetheless that you had had this meeting with Colonel Beara. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have said that Colonel Beara came there and said that he was going to kill all of the prisoners in Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were able to exercise your authority to ensure that those killings did not take place in Bratunac. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, according to your testimony - if we are to believe your testimony - you were able to say, I have an order from President Karadzic, and I'm telling you, Colonel Beara, that there's not going to be any killings. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the evening of the 13th before you went to bed in your safe and sound environment at home, you were under the impression that Colonel Beara had accepted the order that you had given him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But don't be ironic when you're talking about my safe home. Please, could you skip that. My home was as safe as all the other homes were safe at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You weren't boxed up in some warehouse, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the morning of the 14th, you wake up or somebody wakes you up and you learn, according to your testimony, that Colonel Beara is searching for the brick factory in order to put some prisoners over there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the brick factory happens to be in the Bratunac or within the Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again we see your de facto, if not de jure, powers, where you have a confrontation with Beara and you order him out of Bratunac, that there shall be no killings in Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Beara, from what I understand, I've never met the gentleman, but I understand he's a tall man --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to object to the question. It was compound --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He answered the question, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Listen to the objections from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is the danger of a compound question. It had two parts. One, you ordered him out of Bratunac; two, you ordered that there be no killing. Mr. Deronjic naturally, I believe, answered the second part of the question, but we are left with the record that he has ordered Mr. Beara out of Bratunac. And perhaps -- I don't think there's anything in the record. That's why I object to that, and I know Mr. Karnavas understands what the facts are. But now we are left with that on the record. Which is why I decided to stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that might be important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can assure you -- and I thank my learned colleague. But I assure you we were going to get to that. We go from the general to the specific. And we're going to -- this is going to be -- we are going to discuss this. But I thank and appreciate the Prosecution's concern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But let me first describe Beara so we can all have this general description. He's not a small guy like me. He's a pretty big fellow, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he has a pretty formidable appearance, does he not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree for that, but I allow for perhaps you feeling that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the head of the security sector for the Main Staff, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he also had a reputation during the war -- a reputation that follows him all the way here to The Hague, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Please, please, listen to me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I accept your answer. You did not know anything about Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, he probably did have a reputation that you are speaking about. But I said that I never heard about Mr. Beara in my life, nor did I see him before the time he actually came into my office. So I hope that you also -- that this is now clear. And I hope that you also would like to hear the truth come out and for everything to be clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I accept that, that you in your position had never heard of Beara. Fine. Now, you were able to have this confrontation, because it was somewhat confrontational, with Mr. Beara on the 14th of July, the head of a security organ of the VRS army. And you were able to order him not to have any killings in Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were able to order him that those prisoners were not going to go into a facility that was within the Bratunac municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are repeating the question. Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact that is exactly what Beara did. He left angrily, according to you, to your prior testimony. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in spite of him being a military man and despite all orders that he had, presumably from his superior, which would have been Mladic, an order which he had to carry out, at least in his own mind, you, Deronjic, as commissioner and as head of the SDS party were able to exercise your control and order him out of Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I would not allow for those killings to be committed in Bratunac, that I had orders that were different from President Karadzic. But I have one addition. Based on that example, you are trying to construct this idea of some power that I had at that time. There are situations in which a person does not even think of their own powers or the consequences. This was one of such situations. I can tell you any number of situations during the war in which I acted outside of my reasonable powers that I had at the time, but I will not burden you with that. At the time when I found out he was intending to do that, regardless of the fact that I'm not sure who ordered him to do this, I said, Mr. Beara, you cannot do this. This was just a human gesture. At that point, I was not thinking of my powers, reacting early in the morning when I found out. Even though we had reached some kind of an agreement about that, I got the impression that he would not do anything else with the prisoners anymore in Bratunac but would act upon orders of President Karadzic, in the way I conveyed them to Beara. I find out that again he was going over there to see something. So I was very angry at that moment. I got into the car, I got there and I said, Sir, did we not discuss this situation last night? This is out of the question, there can be no detention of people, no killings and please act in accordance with that. At that moment he was there with his security. He could have shot at me. It was possible for him to do that. I was by myself. He could have killed me. But at that point I did not think about that at all. Based on just that one moment, you cannot draw the conclusion that I had some kind of absolute power and that I could also go to Mladic and tell him everything to his face, listen you can do this or you cannot do that or that I'm ordering you to do such-and-such. I think that you are trying to suggest something like, something like a wrong conclusion the way you are going about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was merely pointing an example, just as you did earlier, Mr. Deronjic, but you would agree with me that as a result of your intervention, at least those prisoners of whom you were still responsible for were not killed in Bratunac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're now throwing in that we can discuss it, whether I was responsible or not. You should not be simply asserting that. But it's true that Beara acted in an angry manner, that he left the premises. I waited for a while and I realised that convoys were heading out to Zvornik. Whether he had consulted anyone, well, it is my assumption that he had. He must have asked someone. But again these are just assumptions. He may have said, Yes, take these people to Zvornik, but I cannot know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to discuss more on that evening, what happened on that evening. But I want to get back to where we were, because the chronology is somewhat in dispute, and we still haven't figured this one out. Now, if I can go back to your statement of February 4, 1998, and that's -- and I'm referring for the record to D93/1. At some point you say -- you've indicated in this particular interview, you indicate that in the course of the following day, we've already established this that you stated this, in the course of the following day you had a meeting with Karadzic, that would have been the 12th, if your chronology was correct. And I'm saying if; I'm qualifying that. Now, on the next page, on page, it would be page 4 in the English version. It would be page 3 in your version. You state --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3, line 28. And I'm going to be reading down from there. Actually, let me go further up. Let me start with line 26. In the English version it would be page 4, line 3. One of your tasks, you indicate, and I quote: "I was told to establish contact urgently with all representatives from these three respective formations. With an instruction to inform them on the president's decision to appoint me as someone who should take care about the civilian population in war conditions." You then go on to state, this is line -- it's -- this would be line 28 in your version. "Of course" --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3, sir. We're still on page 3. So I just read from line 26 to line 28. And now you state: "Of course I was requested by President to respect all the conventions established about proper treatment of the civilian population in war conditions." You then go on to state: "Upon my return to the region of Srebrenica, I have asked for an urgent meeting with a Commander Mladic, who was staying there on spot. In addition to a meeting with Mr. Vasic, who was the head of the local police, meaning the centre of public security. I had also invited a commander of the local brigade, of the Bratunac Brigade, to attend at this meeting." And then you go on to state that: "In addition to a local head of the police station, there Mr. Josipovic; Mr. Simic, who was the president of the municipality there; and local president of the municipality government, Mr. Davidovic. So I have informed them with the contents of the order given by Mr. President, by which I was appointed." Now, according to this statement, according to this statement, it states, if we follow your chronology as it was on February 4, before you had the opportunity to meet with your friendly advisors, you're stating that you went to see President Karadzic on the morning of the 12th and then -- or on the 12th. And then sometime later is when you asked to meet with all these representatives in order to convey to them specifically president -- the president's order that all conventions are respected and that proper treatment of civilian population in war conditions. That today we know is not a correct date. Correct? This assessment of yours, this chronology.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, there is -- and for the first time here we also see that you asked to see Mladic, who is of the Main Staff. There is no mentioning of you asking of the Drina Corps commander, either Zivanovic or Krstic, whoever might have been in charge at the time, but instead you state here that you're asked that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade attend this meeting. Now, how was this invitation extended to Colonel Blagojevic? Was it by phone? Was it by fax? Was it by courier? Was it by chance meeting? Or is there another option which I have failed to come up with?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way back -- now we are discussing firm facts, not what I said here because the dates are not accurate. After my conversation with Karadzic on the 11th in the evening, I acted the way it is described here. I tried to gather as many relevant individuals as possible, including political and military individuals, in order to convey to them what Mr. Karadzic had told me over the telephone. I think here that this was -- this had been conveyed to me in person, and this is how I describe it. I also state here all of the individuals that I managed to find. I had contacted the secretary and asked her to try and get in touch with all these people. If you go on on page 5, you will see that I expand on this information, questioned by Mr. Ruez. I state commander Blagojevic once again and say that his competences at the moment were not very large. He was not present at the meeting. Today I know for sure he was not present at the meeting. Furthermore, I was not able to find Mr. Mladic. I know that Commander Krstic was the commander of the operation, but I believed at the time that he was somewhere out in the field, so I wasn't even try to find him. This is all explained in this passage. Those people I was able to find had gathered in my office. And I assume this is what is interesting for you. Today I know for sure that despite the fact that I asked the secretary to find Mr. Blagojevic, he did not attend this meeting. I was able to check this subsequently, and I have firm evidence to prove that he had not attended this meeting. The secretary probably was not able to find him. But at that moment, he was not so important for me, as I state here, because of the presence of a large number of officers at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we were going to get to that, but now since we are on to Mr. Blagojevic with respect to this meeting, you -- it is correct -- as I -- since we're on to Mr. Blagojevic, it is my understanding that you viewed him as someone who was not terribly important. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I believed that he was not necessary with respect of what I had to tell the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bratunac -- the Bratunac Brigade had been going through commanders left and right. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Blagojevic was just the newest commander for the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had just arrived only a few weeks earlier?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, but I don't know the exact date of the appointment. But I think this is correct, based on information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And unlike his, for instance, head of security, Momir Nikolic, he was not the commander of the Territorial Defence during the -- in 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Bratunac. I'm not aware that he was anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's also fair to say that you, by this point in time in history of the events in and around Srebrenica, Bratunac, and what have you, you had solidified your position, which was relatively important, that is that of a -- the head of the SDS party. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I really don't understand what you mean when you say "solidified my position."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you -- we're going to get to your background, but you had moved up the party rank rather rapidly, and once you got to be president, you stayed president. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the Bratunac SDS, but where did I go from there? I became and I remained president --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that was your little fiefdom and we're going to get to that. But what I'm trying to establish is that for several years you had been the president of the SDS. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the municipal branch of the SDS, to avoid confusion. I don't want anyone to think I was the president of the SDS of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that, but you did have the ear of the president of the SDS of Republika Srpska. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either I'm not receiving the right interpretation or I simply cannot believe that I had the ear of the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we'll get to that --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had my ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that. In any event, at this point in time, as you indicate here, given the various VRS units that were located in Bratunac, on the scale of hierarchy, Blagojevic was way down, with Mladic, Zivanovic, Krstic being above him. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now that we clarified that, let me go back to what I was doing, because I want to go back. Now I want to see what you said in relation to this meeting on 21 October 1999, because this is the version that you give months later after you had an opportunity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just an objection. Foundation. I'm not really sure it's been established that there was a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The meeting you're talking about. It hasn't been established that there was a meeting. The direct examination said that that part you just read hasn't happened. And you haven't come to a meeting, so there's no foundation. It's a little confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you could clarify for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did you meet with Mladic -- well, in fact, you did meet with Mladic. You had a breakfast meeting with him. He's eating there and he's sort of disrespecting you and the president of the Republika Srpska. We covered that yesterday. Right? There was a meeting on the 12th, the morning of the 12th, before the official meeting with the Muslim representatives and UNPROFOR in the Hotel Fontana. We covered that yesterday. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we will really have to slow down. I hear incredible things from the interpreters. You're saying that the president of Republika Srpska was at the Fontana Hotel. We really have to correct this. Could you please repeat your question slowly so that I can receive accurate information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the morning of the 12th, there was a meeting at the Hotel Fontana, a breakfast meeting, that was being hosted by General Mladic. You were there. And that was the meeting we talked about where Mladic was disrespecting President Karadzic and you. He was making disparaging [Realtime transcript read in error "^"] remarks, unkind remarks, perhaps even unfounded?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At that meeting, Colonel Blagojevic wasn't there, was he?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact at no time during that period was there ever a meeting where Colonel Blagojevic was present. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase, Your Honour. I know the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Especially the caret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know the objection. I stand corrected

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At no time during the period -- you find it amusing, Mr. Deronjic. Okay. During the time of July 11th and say the 17th when you meet with the representatives of the Muslims. Okay? You are not -- at no time was Mr. Blagojevic in any meeting at which you were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe that was Mr. McCloskey's objection or he wanted some clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct? I need to have a record. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interpretation. I'm waiting for the interpretation. I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas, but you have to bear in mind that when you finish, the interpreters are still continuing with the interpretation. And one other thing, please do not interject things like: You find it amusing, Mr. Deronjic. I smart because an objection was going to be raised and I myself wanted to say this with respect to your question. That is to say, at no meeting that I attended was Mr. Blagojevic present during that period of time, during those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you did indicate, going back to your statement of 21 October 1999, that was the one you had subsequent to your meeting with your friendly connections where you worked on the chronology. And that one, we've established, you had told Mr. Ruez - although we can disagree on whether you were correct or not - but nonetheless you told him then that you went to Pale to meet with President Karadzic on the 11th of July. Do you recall that, having said that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it indicates here that on your return -- you could find this on page 6 of your transcript. But we learn -- you indicate that upon your return you learn that General Mladic held a short meeting in the headquarters of the brigade. It's page 6, line 12 to 22. Your version, it's page 6, lines 11 through 18. This is the area I'm covering.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. Please let me find it. From line 12, this is where it starts in my text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. It says that -- it says: "What time, it was precisely, I wouldn't know. It was after midnight, the very same night." In the previous page, you indicate you had gone that very same day. So we're talking about the night of the 11th going into the 12th. And you state: "The very same night in Bratunac, General Mladic held a sort meeting in the headquarters of the brigade. I did not take part in that meeting simply because I was just in Pale. Last time we talked, I didn't know about this meeting, but following that meeting I inquired about that meeting and I learned about that meeting. From my talks with the president of the municipality, president of the executive board, and some police officials, I learned about meeting, and that's a small alteration to the original." And that I've just read for the record from page 6, lines 11 through 18. And this is from what has been marked for identification as P692. Now, it would seem from this version that you did, in fact, go to Pale on that night, which perhaps may explain why you were not at the meetings in the Fontana on that particular evening. And it also is clear that after you had consulted with your friendly connections, some of whom you've mentioned here who were at that meeting, or at least had informed you of those meetings, you came to the conclusion that you were not at the Hotel Fontana because you were still in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my question is -- the question is: I'm trying to -- the chronology is important and it seems that initially you stated that it was the day after the fall of Srebrenica, being the 12th, that you went to Karadzic. That was at a point in time when you were not clear on the dates. You are then informed that you are a suspect. You are then given an opportunity to meet and caucus with your friendly connections. And after that, you give a statement where you say that you were in Pale the night of the 11th, which is why you could not be there for the meetings that took place at the Hotel Fontana on the night of the 11th. And you also tell us that you learned of these meetings through various folks, some of whom you have today told us are your friendly connections that helped you come up with this chronology. So my question to you is: Are you still maintaining that you did not go to Pale on that -- on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still maintaining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, I'm told that, I guess, apparently this document has two numbers. This is "tehnicki" stuff. It's D95/1. This is for the identification of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I don't want to confuse you. Okay. So your understanding is that you maintain your position. All right. Now, if we go on, if we go on, to page 13 of this same document, one would get the impression that what you're saying -- I'll make references to the particular segment, but please listen to the question first. It appears that what you're telling Mr. Ruez is that you were totally unaware of the attack on Srebrenica. This was something that was arranged at the highest levels. And you say, in fact, "Belgrade, Sarajevo, Pale." If you were to look at page 12, around lines 22 to 26, you would find that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then you say: "I didn't know anything about it." This is line 10 in the English version, page 13. "I didn't know anything about it. Why I didn't know anything about it? As the operation officially started, the Srebrenica operation, I simply went to the front line. I spent all the time with soldiers on the front line. I thought that it concerned some operations that are related with adjustments to the boundaries between Skelani and Milici. And that was a subject we talked about. Many soldiers witnessed -- who witnessed that I spent in their bunker constructions." Now, Mr. Deronjic, do you maintain that when Srebrenica -- the attack on Srebrenica occurred, that you were in a total dark and that you thought that this must be some operation related with adjustments of the boundaries between Skelani and Milici?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maintain today, as I did in my last interview that, with respect to the intentions of the operation to be carried out in and around Srebrenica, I learned about it in mid-May. I didn't know what the objective of the Srebrenica operation was. I talked about the conversation with Karadzic that I had, which I described in my statement. I went to the front line at the very beginning. At the time, preparations were still underway. I do not recall the exact date when I went to Pribicevac. Up until the 8th or the 9th of May, I'm not sure about the date, when I went to Pale to talk to Mr. Karadzic about it, I did not know what exactly the objective of the Srebrenica operation was. I had some assumptions, judging on the situation on the ground, but I did not have any reliable information as to the objective of the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to get to that at some point, I hope. Now, if we go back to the previous page, just to finish one point. On page -- it would be page -- well, it should be the same page for you, page 12, 1 through 13. You state there that: "Last time I expressed thesis -- I told you this thesis, and I think it's correct. No one of the local authorities in Bratunac knew that there would be an operation in Srebrenica." I've just read, for the record, lines 16 to 18. Okay. "No one of the local authorities in Bratunac knew that there would be an operation in Srebrenica." No one, that would mean you as well, would it not, or you did not consider yourself a local authority or a member of the local authority in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can take it however you like. It's known what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then you go on to say: "The reason is that it was a surprise for me, even though I performed the highest functions position at that time. For instance, the president of the municipality at that first day of fall of Srebrenica was in Nis city, for instance, because many troops gathered in Bratunac. So before his departure, he asked me whether it is advisable to go to Nis and what I expected -- what I expect concerning Srebrenica. I told him that there was no reason for him not to go there, because I expect nothing to happen in Srebrenica. Had I known that something would happen, I would never let him go." And then you go on to say: "Luckily he heard about it, he heard about the fall of Srebrenica, and he hurried back." I take it you maintain that this was a truthful and honest statement at the time that you made it and as you stand here today?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the last thing you said, that it was a truthful statement --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An honest statement --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- At the time that you made it. And do you still maintain that it is still today?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that Ljubisav Simic did not know about the operation or about how it would proceed in Srebrenica. And I couldn't assume when they would enter Srebrenica and all the things that would happen in Srebrenica. It was a possibility, but I never mentioned that or discussed that with Ljubisav Simic at all. Particularly in the early stages when I didn't know what the objective of the Srebrenica operation was. He asked me, could he go to Nis. And I said, yes, of course, just do your job, not expecting that anything would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in other words he asked you permission if he could leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to this point. This has been -- this was gone over in depth yesterday, and you may recall there was -- about Mr. Simic going to Nice which has now been cleared as Nis, but this is -- we're going over and over, and if we're talking about all these days here, I would object that we would not go over old ground. This is old ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be heard. Yesterday there was some equivocation with respect to whether he suggested or whether he ordered. And I want to make sure that we're crystal clear and that the record is clear. This is a topic that is dear to Mr. McCloskey's heart and I want to make sure there's no misunderstandings in the record. And that's why I'm asking him now that we have concretely the wording where he says I would have never let him go. I wanted him to be very specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the question I asked, based on his answer was: So President Simic had to ask your permission to go to Nis, correct, based on what you stated here?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. I didn't understand your question. And I'm telling you I'm having difficulty following the continuity in what you are saying because you are skipping from topic to topic. So I don't know what the emphasis is in your questions. It's not correct what is stated stating here and I think you are delving into the semantics too much. Here it states he asked me whether he could go for the trip, but I wasn't paying attention to every word in the interview. In order to explain this, Mr. Karnavas, so that you have a sense of this. I used to go to these meetings by myself. Sometimes there would be five people, sometimes three, sometimes two would be questioning me at the same time. So you can imagine that at that time I would not be paying attention to every single phrase, every single word. So of course it's normal that there are some mistakes, perhaps words that are too forceful, used imprecisely. I agree it's important, that we need to clarify that, and I thank you because you are making it possible for me to clarify what I meant and what I did not mean. If you want to draw certain conclusions from that, tell me which ones and I can tell you whether that is correct or not, whether that corresponds to the truth or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall having -- do you recall being questioned by Mr. Milosevic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at one point, getting back to your conversations, the ones that you indicate occurred sometime on the 9th of July - we haven't gotten to that yet - where you had gone to Pale and -- because you were concerned that the operation with respect to Srebrenica wasn't going well. Do you recall that line of questioning by Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that is correct. I cannot remember everything, but I have no reason to doubt that that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me give you some more clues. Do you recall where you had indicated at some point during this conversation that you were having with Mr. Karadzic, I believe it was a tete-a-tete, four ears, four eyes, nobody else around to verify whether it happened or not. But on that occasion, you spoke with Mr. -- President Karadzic because you wanted to know one -- one of the issues that you wanted to know was what was the real intention with respect to the attack on Srebrenica and at which point President Karadzic told you that there were two options, one of those options being the complete takeover of Srebrenica. Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I remember all of that. But I -- again, you are cuing me. You said at one point that nobody was there, suggesting, of course, that I was making it up, while I precisely that said next to us a few steps away there were Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Krajisnik. These people are still alive. One of them even confirmed that to me. I can talk about that when I testify in some other cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But as far as I read your testimony, at no place in time do you state that they were there having this conversation with you, because as I read your testimony, and we'll get to the specifics, but as I read it, you have indicated that when you went there unannounced to Pale, you took President Karadzic aside or he came -- you walked away and you had a one-on-one conversation with the president. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. It's not correct. Allow me to explain. You really --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will discuss that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled to conduct my cross-examination in the order in which I -- in the order of which -- in the order I wish. Now, I indicated to the gentleman we will discuss that incident in great detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But do not be argumentative with this witness. You are to allow this witness to answer your question, we have to go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
